reason: The cited evidence shows Mo's general strengthening role in Ti alloys and refractory HEAs, but none of the passages demonstrate Mo-rich precipitate formation in a Ti-Ni-primary HEA or the effect of aging on such precipitates. The key premise of precipitation strengthening via Mo-rich precipitates in this specific system is unsupported.
premises: Mo acts as a strong solid-solution strengthener and beta stabilizer in Ti alloys
Mo addition improves elevated-temperature strength in refractory HEAs
Refractory HEAs can form simple solid-solution phases with high-temperature microstructural stability
Precipitation of fine Mo-rich phases can impede dislocation motion and enhance creep resistance
Aging heat treatments can be optimized to form fine precipitates in HEAs
